title: The deep ocean presses with a tonne per square centimetre
body: Pressure rises about one atmosphere every ten metres of seawater; at Challenger Deep, nearly eleven kilometres down, it exceeds a thousand atmospheres, like a small car balanced on a fingernail. Yet animals thrive there, being mostly water themselves with nothing compressible to crush. Engineering visitors need titanium spheres; residents need nothing.
source_hint: Hydrostatic pressure calculation; Trieste and submersible records
